claims.text: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi initially has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The initial FCC/B2 lamellae have incoherent interfaces that act as stress-concentration points.
The untreated Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy is brittle and exhibits isolated microcracks.
The proposed intervention is hexahedron-anvil HPHT treatment at approximately 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
The specified HPHT treatment will transform the lamellae into a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
The specified HPHT treatment will replace incoherent FCC/B2 boundaries with coherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
Pressure can tune alloy phase stability by changing the relative thermodynamic favorability of phases.
The 6 GPa and 1473 K conditions are sufficient to drive the proposed topological transformation while remaining below the threshold for phase instability or eutectic decomposition.
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between adjoining phases.
Dislocation transfer across coherent interfaces alleviates stress concentrations and suppresses interfacial crack initiation.
The transformed structure will activate stacking-fault and twinning deformation mechanisms in addition to dislocation transfer.
The proposed mechanisms will produce a more homogeneous strain distribution.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain after HPHT treatment.
The treated alloy will show elongated rather than isolated crack morphologies on its fracture surface.
Elongated fracture-surface cracks are an indicator of improved ductility in this alloy.
The treated alloy will have a superior strength-ductility combination relative to the untreated baseline.
Conventional thermal-mechanical processing will not produce the same hierarchical interface coherence or GND homogenization as HPHT processing.
The exact pressure-temperature threshold for the proposed topological transformation in Al0.7CoCrFeNi is unknown.
